title: Signal · Wednesday 11 November
overview: Anthropic sets the price range for its IPO, global banks put about USD 270 million behind a joint stablecoin, and Avaloq takes its Mosaic platform to the US.

top.headline: Update: Anthropic starts its IPO roadshow with a USD 70 to 78 price range
top.summary: Anthropic said on 10 November that it had launched the roadshow for its initial public offering of 825 million Class A shares at an expected USD 70 to 78 each, and that it has applied to list on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT. At the top of the range the company would be worth USD 1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis, according to TechCrunch.
top.background: The updated filing adds a USD 26 billion private sale of non-voting shares at the IPO price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC, and gives run-rate revenue of USD 81 billion at the end of October, TechCrunch reported.
top.why: The pricing will test investors' appetite for AI labs after last week's sell-off, and a listed Anthropic will publish audited quarterly figures on a model supplier to a growing number of banks.
top.watch_next: The final price, and the start of trading, which CNBC expects close to 19 November.

top.headline: Goldman, Citi and other banks commit about USD 270 million to a joint stablecoin
top.summary: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank are among the banks committing around USD 270 million to fund five years of operations for a joint dollar stablecoin issuer, Bloomberg reported on 10 November, according to Decrypt. The planned US company, codenamed Project Faro, has no chief executive or final name yet.
top.background: The 21 institutions behind it, including UBS, Lloyds, BBVA, Bank of America and MUFG, committed in September to a launch in the first half of 2027, with a euro version to follow. Tether and Circle hold about 85 percent of a stablecoin market worth roughly USD 290 billion.
top.why: Committed funding turns a consortium plan into an operator with a budget, and UBS's membership puts a Swiss bank inside a bank-led challenge to Tether and Circle.
top.watch_next: Who is named chief executive, and whether JPMorgan, which is not on the list, stays out.

top.headline: Avaloq enters the US wealth market with Mosaic, a modular platform
top.summary: Avaloq said on 10 November that it is entering the US with Avaloq Mosaic, which connects investment data and portfolio processes across wealth managers' existing systems instead of replacing them. It starts with Portfolio IQ, a real-time view of holdings across accounts and custodians, and Allocator for building portfolios at scale, while Agent Connect gives firms' AI tools governed access to verified investment data.
top.background: The NEC-owned Swiss vendor serves more than 170 institutions and has built a US team led by Suzzanna Gill as president. Modules for tax, asset servicing and lending are to follow.
top.why: A layer that works beside the incumbent core is a different sale from a platform replacement, and Agent Connect shows vendors positioning as the governed data route for banks' AI agents.
top.watch_next: The first named US clients, which the announcement does not give.

items.headline: Bern Cantonal Bank folds its IT subsidiary Aity back into the bank from 2028
items.summary: BEKB said on 10 November that Aity, the IT company it formed after taking over its IT from partner DXC, will be fully integrated into the bank on 1 January 2028. The separate structure added complexity and external business grew less than expected, according to finews. Markus Schwab, who has run both since July 2026, will lead the merged IT.
items.why: A cantonal bank conceding that selling its IT to other banks did not pay off is a useful data point for any bank weighing an IT spin-off.

items.headline: Former Alpian chief's Light Frame raises USD 5.1 million for wealth banking software
items.summary: Light Frame, founded in 2024 by former Alpian chief executive Schuyler Weiss, raised USD 5.1 million in a seed round led by Fortino Ventures, according to finews. Its cloud platform links core banking and portfolio management for private banks, asset managers and family offices, with AI at its centre, and the company says it is already in use at unnamed clients.
items.why: Another modular, AI-centred entrant aimed at the gap between core banking and portfolio tools, the same gap Avaloq's Mosaic targets in the US.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley agrees to buy transfer agent Vinyl Equity, eyeing tokenised shares
items.summary: Morgan Stanley has agreed to buy Vinyl Equity, an SEC-registered digital transfer agent founded in 2022, for undisclosed terms. Vinyl will join Morgan Stanley at Work so companies can run cap tables, share plans and transfers in one place, and the bank said the deal lays groundwork for its tokenisation plans. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027.
items.why: Owning the share register brings Morgan Stanley closer to private-company founders and staff before listing, a client pool wealth managers chase as companies stay private longer.

items.headline: UBS Swiss Real Estate Bubble Index eases to 0.64, still in the moderate zone
items.summary: The index fell to 0.64 in the third quarter from 0.71, and UBS still rates the risk moderate, citing the economic recovery and higher household incomes. Prices of owner-occupied homes were 3.5 percent above a year earlier, while asking rents rose 1.7 percent. Imbalances are greatest in Graubünden's tourist regions and the city of Zurich, according to finews.
items.why: Mortgages dominate cantonal and regional bank balance sheets, and UBS expects demand for owner-occupied homes to hold up in 2027 despite the rate rises it anticipates.

items.headline: Norway's wealth fund puts the UBS-occupied Üetlihof in Zurich back up for sale
items.summary: Norway's sovereign wealth fund has started a new sale of the Üetlihof, the former Credit Suisse office complex in Zurich, and wants a deal before the end of the year, according to the NZZ, cited by finews. UBS's lease runs until 2037 with options to extend by up to 15 years, and UBS is offering about 14,600 square metres for sublet.
items.why: The sublet space shows the Credit Suisse integration has changed UBS's office needs in Zurich, even as it moves teams from other sites into the complex.

items.headline: Lucerne backs LUKB chief's move to the board; FINMA sets a cooling-off year
items.summary: The Lucerne government sees no governance problem in chief executive Daniel Salzmann joining Luzerner Kantonalbank's board in April 2027, months after he steps down at the end of 2026, according to finews, citing the Luzerner Zeitung. FINMA requires a one-year cooling-off period in which he may not sit on board committees or become chair or vice chair.
items.why: FINMA's conditions show how the supervisor treats a chief executive moving straight to the board, a question other cantonal banks face in their own successions.

items.headline: Affirm agrees to buy Ratepay from Nexi, adding pay-by-invoice in German-speaking markets
items.summary: US payment network Affirm will acquire Ratepay, the German pay-by-invoice provider serving merchants in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, from Italy's Nexi, which is focusing on its core activities. The two also signed a memorandum to widen their partnership in the region. Regulatory approvals are expected in the first half of 2027.
items.why: Puts a US buy now, pay later lender behind an invoice payment service that Swiss merchants already use, raising the stakes for local instalment providers.

items.headline: Barclays opens a Riyadh office under a Saudi licence and names a local CEO
items.summary: Barclays has opened an office in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District after Saudi Arabia's Capital Market Authority licensed it for investment banking and global markets business, WealthBriefing reported on 10 November. Majed Al Hassoun, previously chief executive of State Street Saudi Arabia, leads the local entity, Barclays Capital Saudi.
items.why: A local licence lets Barclays cover Saudi corporate, government and institutional clients from Riyadh, with a chief executive who also deals with the regulators.

items.headline: Update: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers at Argon's price
items.summary: Two weeks after giving it to cyber defenders, Google made Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, available on 10 November to paying developers and enterprises, at Argon's introductory price of USD 2 per million input tokens and USD 10 per million output tokens. Google is also previewing a swarm feature in Antigravity that turns one prompt into a team of agents.
items.why: Frontier capability at a mid-tier price lowers the cost case for long, multi-step agent work such as code migration and document review.

items.headline: Anthropic adds Claude Meetings, Whiteboards and Sheets as AI labs build office suites
items.summary: Claude Meetings, in beta on Team and Enterprise plans, joins Google Meet calls as a visible participant and drafts plans and timelines while people talk, according to TechCrunch. It will not join calls with external guests unless an admin allows it. Claude Sheets, in beta on paid plans, builds working spreadsheets, and Claude Data is now generally available.
items.why: An AI participant in calls raises recording, consent and confidentiality questions that banks' compliance teams will want settled before any rollout.

items.headline: OpenAI launches a Business Hub so companies can manage how ChatGPT presents them
items.summary: OpenAI's Business Hub, in beta, lets companies create verified profiles of their products and services, launch a business agent that answers users' questions, and see limited insights such as profile views, mentions and website clicks, TechCrunch reported on 10 November. OpenAI retired its in-chat checkout effort in March.
items.why: Financial firms will need to decide who verifies and maintains what ChatGPT says about their products, a question for marketing and compliance alike.

items.headline: Databricks now publishes Unity Catalog metric views straight into Power BI semantic models
items.summary: Databricks said on 10 November that metrics defined once in Unity Catalog metric views can be published directly to Power BI semantic models, from Catalog Explorer or a Power BI task that keeps them in sync. Unity Catalog access controls stay in place with DirectQuery, so Power BI, AI/BI dashboards and Genie return the same figures.
items.why: For banks running Power BI on a Databricks lakehouse, one governed definition of a metric removes a source of conflicting figures between finance, risk and AI tools.

say_it_today: Avaloq's US launch and Light Frame's new round rest on the same bet: wealth managers will modernise around their core systems rather than replace them.
